To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the traffic features of contemporary standalone DoS attack samples differ considerably from the traffic of the attacks that were used for the development of contemporary DoS attack detection methods.

(1) the most common attack features, such as packet size, are used for evasion; (2) the most common anomaly is packet loss; and (3) the most common evasion technique is the use of multiple attack sources.
the attack traffic features are diverse and the attack detection should take this into account.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of traffic features generated by standalone DoS attack tool.

the analysis of traffic features that were generated by the following standalone DoS attack software: slowloris, hping3, slowhttptest, slowhttptest2, slowhttptest3 and slowhttptest4, as well as the analysis of traffic patterns that are characteristic for the DoS attacks.

the following: (i) the analysis and classification of DoS attack traffic features that were generated by standalone DoS attack tool, (ii) the analysis of DoS attacks traffic features and the proposed research direction for the DoS attacks detection at the source end.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the traffic generated by standalone attack tools is not representative for the real world attacks.
there is still a lack of reliable data for the DoS detection research.

the detection of Do S attacks is not a solved problem, as it is commonly assumed, but rather a very challenging task, especially in the case of modern attacks that are capable of bypassing the most advanced detection mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DoS attacks generated by state-of-art standalone tools are highly diversified and that the majority of them can be recognized by the use of machine learning methods.
the DoS attack detection methods should be verified on the traffic samples generated by contemporary attack tools.
the DoS attacks are still a serious threat and that the research community should be aware of their evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

DoS attacks are becoming more and more complex and stealthy, and therefore the research community should focus more on the development of detection methods based on deep learning techniques, rather than on simple anomaly detection methods.
the DoS attack traffic can be classified into four main categories based on the attack tool and the attack type.
the DoS attack traffic is not random, it is rather repetitive and predictable.
